Fit named pieces of text into a token budget under a context policy

Source: R/core-context-policy.R
hr_context_fit.Rd

When the pieces together are longer than budget tokens, cuts them under policy (hr_context_policy()): pinned pieces are never cut; the pieces in cut_order are cut first, in order, and then the others, the last piece first. Each piece is cut only as far as the total needs, by hr_truncate() with the piece's keep rule, and a piece that must go entirely becomes "". Each cut is written to trace as a "truncate" step with where set to "<where>.<piece>".

Usage

hr_context_fit(
  pieces,
  budget,
  policy = hr_context_policy(),
  scores = NULL,
  trace = NULL,
  where = "context"
)

Arguments

pieces

A named character vector (or a named list of single strings), in the order the request carries them.

budget

The most tokens the pieces may hold together.

policy

An hr_context_policy().

scores

For pieces cut with keep = "scored": a list of score vectors named by piece. A piece without scores is cut with "head".

trace

Optional gr_trace.

where

The packer's name, the start of each cut's where.

Value

A list of pieces (named character, in the order given), fits (whether they now fit; FALSE when the pinned pieces alone do not), tokens (their total), cut (the names of the pieces cut) and tokens_dropped.

See also

hr_context_policy(), hr_truncate()

Other cost and token functions: hr_budget(), hr_context_policy(), hr_count_tokens(), hr_estimate_cost(), hr_load_models(), hr_model_info(), hr_model_limits(), hr_models(), hr_register_model(), hr_set_tokenizer(), hr_tokenizer(), hr_truncate(), hr_truncate_tokens()

Examples

pieces <- c(question = "What was revenue?",
            draft = paste(rep("Revenue rose.", 30), collapse = " "),
            excerpt = paste(rep("Costs fell.", 30), collapse = " "))
fit <- hr_context_fit(pieces, 80, hr_context_policy(pin = c("question", "draft")))
vapply(fit$pieces, hr_count_tokens, numeric(1))
#> question    draft  excerpt 
#>        7       93        0 
fit$cut
#> [1] "excerpt"
